label: Daily Recap
periodEnd: Thu, Nov 12, 2026, 4:00 PM ET (that day's close)
timezoneNote: All times below are shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks slipped after the sudden ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent shockwaves through the technology sector (4:26 PM ET), and WSJ reported Nvidia tumbled while AMD and Broadcom advanced and yields rose (4:11 PM ET). Bloomberg reported that Wall Street was not particularly concerned about the risk to the AI trade from Huang's exit (4:37 PM ET), and MarketWatch reported the S&P 500 was shrugging off Nvidia's selloff (4:08 PM ET). On the AI side, Bloomberg reported Cisco raised its annual outlook and gave a current-quarter sales forecast above Wall Street estimates (4:17 PM ET), and WSJ reported Applied Materials posted a fourth-quarter profit of $2.72 billion on AI-driven chip demand (4:23 PM ET). On rates, MarketWatch reported fears of more Fed rate hikes were driving yields higher (3:44 PM ET), Bloomberg reported San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further rate increases will likely be needed (2:31 PM ET) and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said inflation is 'inching' into a tough spot (2:36 PM ET), and WSJ reported gold futures fell to more than a one-year low as the dollar and yields rose (2:36 PM ET). WSJ reported oil futures rebounded after President Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran (4:01 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

cryptoDriver.text: The Block reported bitcoin fell to a 12-week low as Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia rattled markets and MSCI confirmed Strategy's removal from its indexes, with about $750 million in crypto positions liquidated (12:40 PM ET). CoinDesk reported spot bitcoin ETF outflows reached a fifth day (6:30 AM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

items.headline: Nvidia files 8-K: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO and director; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: In a Form 8-K (Items 5.02 and 9.01, accepted 8:52 AM ET), Nvidia said its Board accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer and director effective immediately on November 11, 2026. The Board appointed Executive Vice President and CFO Colette M. Kress, age 59, as interim CEO while she continues as CFO, and appointed director Harvey C. Jones, age 73, as Chair, while it searches for a new CEO. The stock closed down 4.34% on Nov 12.

items.headline: Jensen Huang Has Been Ousted as Nvidia CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, Huang resigned after two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, shares in the chipmaker slid after the group said chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim head. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's stock selloff may be just beginning, even after shedding 30% from its peak
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, while Nvidia shares look cheap on paper and on the charts, Wall Street analysts see more volatility ahead. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia, AI Industry Face Prospect of Future Without Huang
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia is expected to survive the ouster, but questions remain about whether it can thrive without Huang's relationships with global leaders and with no predetermined successor. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Top Democrats Target Trump Administration’s Nvidia-China Records
items.summary: Per WSJ, Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked that documents be preserved, often an initial step before formal congressional investigations. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: China warns US not to use Nvidia scandal as pretext for tech curbs
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, Beijing accuses the US of fabricating "espionage narratives" as the chip company's board considers the future of CEO Jensen Huang. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Disappearing Singapore Sales Deepen Mystery Around Megaspeed
items.summary: Per WSJ, last year, just as scrutiny of Megaspeed was rising, Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore revenue. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for CEO Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nasdaq futures fall as Nvidia sinks 8% after hours on report board may oust Huang
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, stock futures slid Wednesday evening as the selloff in Nvidia shares after the close weighed on the Nasdaq-100 and dragged down other chip makers. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
